query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 0.5 wt% boron via arc melting, followed by hot isostatic pressing (HIP) at 1000°C, 100 MPa, for 2 hours, and subsequent aging at an optimized temperature and time, will improve the performance of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state
generation.intervention: Addition of 0.5 wt% boron via arc melting, followed by hot isostatic pressing (HIP) at 1000°C, 100 MPa, for 2 hours
generation.conditions: Subsequent aging at an optimized temperature and time to precipitate boride phases
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of boride precipitates within the lamellar microstructure
generation.mechanism: Precipitation hardening, grain refinement, and improved corrosion resistance due to the boride phases
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and room-temperature creep resistance, with improved corrosion resistance in 3.5% NaCl solution
generation.baseline: The starting alloy's strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements
generation.boundary: Fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions
generation.uncertainty: The optimized aging temperature and time need to be determined to minimize the degradation of the lamellar microstructure while still precipitating boride phases

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing, creep testing, and corrosion testing of the alloy after the intervention
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy's performance does not improve as predicted, the hypothesis is falsified

proposals.intervention: Introduction of 1.5 wt% TiC nanoparticles via mechanical alloying
proposals.conditions: Consolidation via spark plasma sintering at 900°C, 50 MPa, for 5 minutes, followed by aging at 600°C for 24 hours
proposals.structural_mediator: Formation of coherent TiC nanoparticle dispersions within the lamellar microstructure
proposals.mechanism: Orowan strengthening, grain refinement, and improved corrosion resistance due to the TiC nanoparticles
proposals.predicted_outcome: Enhanced yield strength by 15%, ultimate tensile strength by 20%, and room-temperature creep resistance by a factor of 3, with improved corrosion resistance in 3.5% NaCl solution
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: The introduction of TiC nanoparticles addresses the limitations of the starting alloy by providing additional strengthening mechanisms, improving corrosion resistance, and enhancing thermal stability, making it suitable for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, and corrosive conditions

proposals.intervention: High-pressure torsion (HPT) processing at 5 GPa, 10 turns, and room temperature
proposals.conditions: Subsequent annealing at 400°C for 1 hour to relieve residual stresses
proposals.structural_mediator: Grain refinement to the nanoscale and introduction of high-density dislocations
proposals.mechanism: Grain boundary strengthening, dislocation hardening, and improved strain rate sensitivity
proposals.predicted_outcome: Increased yield strength by 25%, ultimate tensile strength by 30%, and improved room-temperature creep resistance by a factor of 4
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: HPT processing and subsequent annealing address the limitations of the starting alloy by providing significant grain refinement, dislocation hardening, and improved strain rate sensitivity, making it suitable for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations and long-term mechanical loading

proposals.intervention: Surface modification via plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) in a silicate-based electrolyte
proposals.conditions: PEO treatment at 300 V, 10 kHz, for 30 minutes, followed by sealing in a vacuum at 200°C for 2 hours
proposals.structural_mediator: Formation of a thick, porous, and adherent oxide layer with improved corrosion resistance
proposals.mechanism: Improved corrosion resistance due to the barrier effect of the oxide layer, and enhanced mechanical properties due to the residual compressive stresses
proposals.predicted_outcome: Enhanced corrosion resistance in 3.5% NaCl solution by a factor of 5, and improved room-temperature creep resistance by a factor of 2
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: The PEO surface modification addresses the limitations of the starting alloy by providing a corrosion-resistant oxide layer, improving the overall corrosion resistance and mechanical properties, making it suitable for fasteners exposed to corrosive conditions
